We need to produce a completed test class for Position.getPositionCost(int). Use JUnit 5. Need to set up dependencies: Position constructors, CostModel (transaction and holding). The method uses transactionCostModel.calculate(this, finalIndex) and getHoldingCost(finalIndex). So we must test that getPositionCost returns sum of transaction cost and holding cost.

We can mock CostModel to control transactionCost and holdingCost via Position's private fields? transactionCostModel is a final field; holdingCostModel is used in getHoldingCost, but that method likely uses holdingCostModel to calculate. In Position we don't see getHoldingCost implementation, but we can assume it uses holdingCostModel.calculate(...). However we cannot rely on internal details. Instead we can create a Position with known transaction and holding models that produce deterministic values, e.g., LinearTransactionCostModel with rate 0.01 and LinearBorrowingCostModel with rate 0.001, then compute expected cost manually using formulas. But we may not know formulas of these models. Safer to mock CostModel and also mock holding cost model? There is no way to inject holdingCostModel separately; Position constructor takes both transactionCostModel and holdingCostModel. So we can pass mocked CostModel for transaction, and another mocked CostModel for holding? Actually the constructor takes CostModel transactionCostModel and CostModel holdingCostModel. So we can provide mocks for both. Then we can stub their calculate methods to return predetermined Num values. Need to use Mockito to mock CostModel and Num.

Num is an interface, but there are concrete implementations like DoubleNum. For easier, we can use DoubleNum.valueOf.

Implementation: mock CostModel transactionMock; mock CostModel holdingMock; stub when(transactionMock.calculate(any(Position.class), eq(finalIndex))).thenReturn(DoubleNum.valueOf(5)); similarly holdingMock.calculate(any(Position.class), eq(finalIndex)).thenReturn(DoubleNum.valueOf(3)); However getHoldingCost(finalIndex) might call holdingCostModel.calculate(this, finalIndex) or there is a method getHoldingCost that uses holdingCostModel. We don't have its code, but likely. So we stub holdingMock.

Create Position position = new Position(TradeType.BUY, transactionMock, holdingMock);

Now we need a trade? Position with starting type BUY but no entry yet; transactionCostModel.calculate will be called even if position not opened? It probably calculates based on entry/exit and finalIndex. It's okay.

Call Num cost = position.getPositionCost(10);

Assert that cost equals DoubleNum.valueOf(8) (5+3). Use assertEquals with DoubleNum equality? There's assertNumEquals method but not imported. But we can use assertEquals(DoubleNum.valueOf(8), cost); But DoubleNum overrides equals? maybe it does. Use assertEquals for simplicity.

Also test scenario where transaction model returns NaN? But not needed.

Also test that if transactionCostModel throws exception? Not required.

Add imports for DoubleNum, Num, TradeType.

Need @BeforeEach to init mocks and position.

Use MockitoAnnotations.openMocks? With MockitoExtension, fields annotated with @Mock will be injected. Let's declare @Mock CostModel transactionModel; @Mock CostModel holdingModel; Then in setupBeforeEach, create position. Also need finalIndex variable.

Write test method: testGetPositionCostReturnsSum.

Potential second test: verify that calculate on both models is called exactly once with correct parameters.

Add verification using Mockito.verify.
